newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has stepped in to end the escalating conflict between the judiciary and the Council of State over an administrative court. Judicial officials have continued their attack on the council, which is the government's legal advisory body, for seeking to control the new court. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- A special panel of members of parliament has been set up to look into the alleged execution of six suspected drug dealers. The Lower House has unanimously voted to establish a 27-member extraordinary committee to examine the facts of the shootings, which shocked the nation last November. The committee has 60 days to carry out its investigation. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- More than 1,000 illegal immigrants have been rounded up in Songkhla province in a major operation triggered by Malaysia's crackdown against illegal foreign workers. Majority of those arrested were Pakistani, Indian, Burmese and Bangladeshi nationals. Most of the arrests took place at factories and construction sites. (THE NATION)

- The budget cut for fiscal 1997 may eventually total 80 billion baht from an earlier targetted amount of 50 billion baht due to less income tax being collected by concerned government agencies, says Deputy Finance Minister Thawatwong na Chiang Mai. The budget cut is aimed at slashing current account deficit. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has pledged to award the two remaining banking licences to finance companies during this year. But some finance companies will have to merge in order to create groups big enough to operate commercial banks. He says details of the new licences will require further consideration by the Bank of Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)

- More high-volume oil traders will be encouraged to set up their own refineries in order to stabilise the country's energy supply and stimulate competition. Only seven of Thailand's 26 oil trading companies have their own refineries. The state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand, the market leader, is among those being prodded to build its own refinery. (BANGKOK POST)
